data.narrative:
Aalo Atomics is a Series B nuclear energy company that has raised $300M+ to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comparative universe of 11 peers across nuclear energy: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Valar Atomics, Helion, Oklo, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised of $300M as a baseline value proxy, application of a typical Series B to next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.9x implies a valuation of $570M. The Peer-Median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow-set comparables: while six same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier companies yielded fewer than the three datapoints required for statistical confidence. A broad all-sector median would introduce material distortion.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $484M to $656M, with a median point estimate of $570M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty given the limited peer dataset and the nascent stage of commercial deployment across the nuclear energy sector. Key variables affecting the range include the magnitude of capital efficiency relative to later-stage peers, timeline to revenue inflection, and regulatory pathway clarity. Additional data on revenue traction or pathway-specific milestones would refine the estimate materially.
